function: Near-field multiuser beam training: GNN maps far-field wide-beam gains of all users to each user's best near-field codeword for hybrid beamforming (p. 6, p. 9).
system: TDD mmWave XL-MIMO, BS ULA 256 antennas, 8 single-antenna users, hybrid precoding with K RF chains, near-field, 30 GHz, 10 MHz; no RIS (p. 3, p. 12).
method: Supervised GNN classifiers (mean aggregation, concatenation, 3 layers) with separate angle and distance networks; labels from exhaustive search; offline training with Adam, online estimation (p. 7-9, p. 12).
data_channel: Wireless InSite ray tracing of a self-built 40x30x5 m smart-factory scene at 30 GHz; 12,000 channel samples, 90% training, 10% testing (p. 12).
test_conditions: K=8 users, 90/10 split; tested over power sweeps and K=1 to 9 users; GNN claimed to need no retraining when K changes (p. 3, p. 12, p. 15).
baselines: Non-learned: exhaustive near-field search, OMP-based scheme; learned: FC network [16], CNN [17]; joint-training GNN is the paper's own variant (p. 12, p. 13).
metrics: Sum rate, effective sum rate with pilot overhead, codeword estimation accuracy, pilot overhead, parameter counts (p. 12, p. 13).
complexity: Overall O(KV N_BS/M + KV^2 L_G + KV N_BS + KV S + K^3); GNN feature module 9.83e4 parameters, output 4.91e4/1.7e4 (Table I) (p. 11, p. 13).
q1_support: p. 12: "we utilized the WI software to create a wireless communication scenario resembling a large smart factory". Ray tracing of a scene built by the authors; not 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 3: "this meritorious GNN is not required to be retrained when the number of users changes"; p. 12: training setup "BS equipped with NBS = 256 antennas serves K = 8" single-antenna users; p. 15: "we evaluate the performance of the proposed GNN-based scheme for different numbers of users" (K = 1 to 9, Figs. 11 and 13).
q3_support: p. 12-13: benchmarks "Exhaustive Near-Field Search", "OMP-Based Scheme" (non-learned), "FC Neural Network-Based Scheme [16]" and "CNN-Based Scheme [17]" (learned). p. 13: "our proposed scheme exhibits significantly better performance than the other benchmark schemes in terms of the sum rate".
q4_support: p. 11: "we quantify the computational complexity of the proposed three-phase GNN-based beam training scheme", giving an overall order; Table I on p. 13 lists the number of parameters (9.83 x 10^4 for the GNN feature module).
q5_support: p. 12: "we utilized the WI software to create a wireless communication scenario resembling a large smart factory". Data are generated by the authors; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 3: the learned part is the GNN codeword selection; the beam allocation (Algorithm 2) and the ZF/MMSE digital precoder are not learned. No RIS in the system model (RIS appears only in cited works [27], [36]). q1 is 0 because the factory scene is built by the authors in a commercial ray tracer, not DeepMIMO or 3GPP; the reviewer may confirm. q2 is inferred from the no-retraining claim plus the K = 1 to 9 sweep against training at K = 8; no single sentence states that the K = 8 model was reused.
